title: Public-repo audit: README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, metadata, and a read-only git-history review
description:
Public-repo audit, authorized by the orchestrator (opum-agent) after 0.6.0's release closed, per a user decision relayed via the orchestrator: audit quest-cli as a public repository (README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, etc., coordinated with lore-cli) and separately review (read-only) git history.

Scope, per opum-agent: README.md (was missing entirely -- the most visible gap on a published package), LICENSE/CONTRIBUTING.md/SECURITY.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, .gitignore correctness, issue/PR templates, repo topics/description/homepage, package.json publish surface (files/repository/bugs/homepage/keywords), and a read-only git-history review for credential shapes, internal hostnames, personal paths, and large blobs.

Coordinated directly with lore-cli: their README/LICENSE/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTING/CODE_OF_CONDUCT/issue-PR-templates are the reference structure (pulled from https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli), adapted rather than copied where quest's actual contract differs.

History rewrite is explicitly NOT in scope -- reserved for this session's own user's direct authorization, and the read-only scan found nothing warranting one regardless (no live secrets found).

acceptanceCriteria.text: README.md exists and covers install, quickstart, the actor-declaration write contract, and links to docs -- matched to lore-cli's reference structure where genuinely parallel
LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and issue/PR templates exist, coordinated with lore-cli

GitHub repo description, homepage, and topics are accurate and set (not stale/empty); package.json publish surface (homepage, bugs, keywords, files) is correct and the published tarball actually contains what it should
A read-only git-history scan for credential shapes, internal hostnames, personal paths, and large blobs is complete and findings are reported, with no unauthorized history mutation

implementationNotes: PR docs/QCLI-260-public-repo-audit#TBD: README.md/SECURITY.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md/issue+PR templates added, structure coordinated directly with lore-cli (fetched their live files as reference). package.json gained homepage/bugs/keywords/files README entry, verified via npm pack --dry-run that the tarball now actually contains the README. GitHub repo description/homepage/topics fixed via API (were stale/empty/null); secret scanning + push protection + Dependabot security updates enabled (were disabled). Read-only git-history scan (separate agent) found no credential-shaped strings, no internal hostnames, no personal-data leaks beyond commit lines -- one low-priority cosmetic item (5 hardcoded local usernames in dated docs/ prose) noted, not fixed. No history mutation performed.
finalSummary:
Public-repo audit complete, landed as PR #350 (squash-merged to dev, 8a0a747) plus a fix-forward commit source-gates itself caught (check-package-artifacts.mjs's hardcoded root-file allowlist needed README.md added). Coordinated directly with lore-cli: pulled their live README/LICENSE/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTING/CODE_OF_CONDUCT/issue-PR-templates as the reference structure, adapted to quest's actual contract (actor-declaration write requirement as the headline, not a Backlog.md coupling; SECURITY documents quest has zero credential surface, verified via grep across src/).

Live GitHub/npm metadata fixed via API (reversible settings, done outside the PR): stale repo description replaced, homepage set to questgraph.dev (matching package.json's new homepage field), topics set (shared half matching lore-cli, plus quest-specific ones), secret scanning + push protection + Dependabot security updates enabled (were all disabled).

Read-only git-history scan (separate agent, full history all branches): no HIGH PRIORITY findings -- no live/credential-shaped secrets anywhere (common token prefixes, private-key blocks, .env/credential filenames all checked; only hits were false positives -- Bun's bundled CA cert store and Bun's own token-redaction code). No internal hostnames. No personal-email leaks beyond commit lines. One LOW PRIORITY cosmetic item noted, not fixed: 5 hardcoded /Users/jdnewhouse/... paths in dated docs/ prose. No history mutation performed, and nothing found argues for a rewrite.

Two items deliberately left as findings rather than fixes, for the orchestrator/user: (1) LICENSE copyright-holder mismatch between quest-cli ("opum-ai") and lore-cli ("Jeremy Newhouse") -- a judgment call, not mine to silently pick a side on; (2) the .gitignore's npm/quest-*/bin/quest* line is currently dead code (files are always committed) but left alone since it's entangled with QCLI-259's open build-fresh-vs-commit architecture question.
